Medium Affected: WATER

Skytruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 42.014354, -93.458765 (Approximated from CITY_STATE)
Reported Spill Volume: 5 gallons
Report Description
AT ~1500 HOURS ON 10/8/11 A PASSENGER VEHICLE LEFT THE ROADWAY 1 1/2 MILES EAST OF 670TH AVE. WHILE ON 180TH ST. NEAR NEVADA, IA. THE VEHICLE ENTERED INDIAN CREEK IN STORY COUNTY IOWA. FIRST RESPONDERS IDENTIFIED A PETRO SHEEN ON THE SURFACE OF INDIAN CREEK. ABSORBENT BOOMS WERE PUT IN PLACE UPSTREAM AND DOWNSTREAM OF THE VEHICLE. Nearest City: Ketchikan, AK

Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: USCGC ANTHONY PETIT
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Sheen Size: 5 feet by 100 feet (area 500 sq. ft.)
Reported Spill Volume: 4 gallons
Skytruth Minimum Possible Spill Volume: 0.01 gallons
CUTTER CREW DRAINED OIL FROM ON BOARD ENGINES THEN PROCEEDED TO TRANSFER THIS OIL INTO THEIR USED OIL TANK. ENGINE ROOM CREW MEMBER FLIPPED A TRANSFER SWITCH ON A VALVE USED TO DIVERT FLUIDS DURING PUMPING OPERATIONS FROM ONE TANK TO ANOTHER. SEVERAL MINUTES LATER THE QUARTER DECK WATCHSTANDER NOTIFIED ENGINEERS OF A SHEEN OFF PORT SIDE. THE DUTY ENGINEERS STOPPED THE INTERNAL TRANSFER OPERATIONS WENT ON-DECK TO DISCOVER OIL MIXTURE EXITING THROUGH THE USED OIL TANK PORT VENT PIPE. MAJORITY OF OIL CAPTURED IN THE SCUPPER, ESTIMATED THAT 2 GALLONS OVER SPILLED SCUPPER INTO WATER. SHIP PERSONNEL NOTIFIED SHORE SIDE SPILL RESPONSE COORDINATOR THEN CONTINUED WITH CONTAINMENT AND CLEANUP.

ON JANUARY 19, 2010 3 BARRELS OR 126 GALLONS OF REFINED PETROLEUM PRODUCTS (GASOLINE) WAS RELEASED FROM A ONE-HALF INCH PRESSURE TRANSMITTER LINE INSIDE EXPLORER PIPELINE’S WOOD RIVER TANK FARM IN MADISON COUNTY, ILLINOIS. ALL THE RELEASED PRODUCT WAS CONTAINED WITHIN THE TERMINAL. TWO BARRELS OR 84 GALLONS OF FREE PHASE PRODUCT WAS RECOVERED. THE REMAINING 1 BARREL OR 42 GALLONS WAS CONTAINED IN THE EXCAVATED SOIL. IT HAS BEEN DETERMINED THAT THAT COST ASSOCIATED WITH THE RELEASE WILL EXCEED $50,000 DUE TO THE LABOR AND SOIL DISPOSAL. THEREFORE, UNDER 49 CFR PART 195.52(A)(3) EXPLORER PIPELINE IS NOTIFYING THE NRC AND PHMSA THAT THE COST FOR THE INCIDENT WILL EXCEED $50,000.

properties.summary: Incident Type: FIXED - NRC Report ID: 953017 - Medium Affected: AIR - Suspected Responsible Party: WESTERN REFINING SOUTHWEST, IN
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 953017
Incident Time: 2010-09-02 20:00:00
Nearest City: Jamestown, NM
Incident Type: FIXED
Material: SULFUR DIOXIDE
Medium Affected: AIR
Suspected Responsible Party: WESTERN REFINING SOUTHWEST, IN
Skytruth Analysis
THE WESTERN REFINING SOUTHWEST, INC. REFINERY LOCATED NEAR GALLUP, NEW MEXICO EXPERIENCED AN EMISSION OF SULFUR DIOXIDE TO THE AIR THAT EXCEEDED THE 500 POUND 24-HOUR EPCRA REPORTABLE QUANTITY (RQ). THE EMISSION OF THE REPORTABLE QUANTITY OF SULFUR DIOXIDE OCCURRED ON THURSDAY, SEPTEMBER 2, 2010. SULFUR DIOXIDE IS EMITTED NORMALLY FROM THE REFINERY FLARE AND HEATERS AND BOILERS USING REFINERY FUEL GAS AS FUEL. REFINERY FUEL GAS IS PRODUCED IN THE REFINERY’S PROCESSES AND ROUTED TO THE REFINERY HEATERS AND BOILERS FOR HEATING AND STEAM GENERATION. SULFUR THAT IS NORMALLY FOUND IN THE FUEL GAS IS COMBUSTED IN THE REFINERY’S HEATERS AND BOILERS FORMING SULFUR DIOXIDE THAT IS EMITTED FROM THE HEATER AND BOILER STACKS. THE QUANTITY OF SULFUR IN THE FUEL GAS WAS SOMEWHAT HIGHER THAN IS NORMALLY THE CASE ON THURSDAY BECAUSE THE REFINERY EXPERIENCED A MALFUNCTION IN THE REFINERY FUEL GAS SYSTEM. THE AMOUNT OF SULFUR DIOXIDE THAT WAS EMITTED EXCEEDING THE 500 POUND RQ THRESHOLD WAS 272 POUNDS. THE REFINERY SUCCEEDED IN RESTORING THE REFINERY FUEL GAS SYSTEM BACK TO NORMAL CONDITIONS LATER IN THE AFTERNOON.

THE WESTERN REFINING SOUTHWEST, INC. REFINERY LOCATED NEAR GALLUP, NEW MEXICO EXPERIENCED AN EMISSION OF SULFUR DIOXIDE TO THE AIR THAT EXCEEDED THE 500 POUND 24-HOUR EPCRA REPORTABLE QUANTITY (RQ). THE EMISSION OF THE REPORTABLE QUANTITY OF SULFUR DIOXIDE OCCURRED ON THURSDAY, SEPTEMBER 2, 2010. SULFUR DIOXIDE IS EMITTED NORMALLY FROM THE REFINERY FLARE AND HEATERS AND BOILERS USING REFINERY FUEL GAS AS FUEL. REFINERY FUEL GAS IS PRODUCED IN THE REFINERY’S PROCESSES AND ROUTED TO THE REFINERY HEATERS AND BOILERS FOR HEATING AND STEAM GENERATION. SULFUR THAT IS NORMALLY FOUND IN THE FUEL GAS IS COMBUSTED IN THE REFINERY’S HEATERS AND BOILERS FORMING SULFUR DIOXIDE THAT IS EMITTED FROM THE HEATER AND BOILER STACKS. THE QUANTITY OF SULFUR IN THE FUEL GAS WAS SOMEWHAT HIGHER THAN IS NORMALLY THE CASE ON THURSDAY BECAUSE THE REFINERY EXPERIENCED A MALFUNCTION IN THE REFINERY FUEL GAS SYSTEM. THE AMOUNT OF SULFUR DIOXIDE THAT WAS EMITTED EXCEEDING THE 500 POUND RQ THRESHOLD WAS 272 POUNDS. THE REFINERY SUCCEEDED IN RESTORING THE REFINERY FUEL GAS SYSTEM BACK TO NORMAL CONDITIONS LATER IN THE AFTERNOON.
